evidence_used: Visual appearance of a ceramic sherd object
Textured and rough visible surface condition reducing gecko pad adhesion
Rigid parallel-jaw gecko gripper embodiment context requiring flat, smooth parallel sidewalls for optimal adhesion
Small to medium visual scale of the object
calculation_summary: Force estimated based on qualitative visual compatibility: F_base (2.0 N) + penalty for surface texture and non-ideal geometry (3.5 N) = 5.5 N.
assumptions_and_uncertainty: No authoritative mass or roughness measurement is available; visual inspection is an approximation.
Object sidewalls are assumed to offer poor mating surface for rigid gecko pads, leading to lower adhesion and higher normal force requirements.
Uncertainty in exact weight and coefficient of friction.
reasoning_trace: The object is a small ceramic sherd with a visibly textured and rough surface. The gecko gripper relies heavily on clean, smooth, flat surfaces to maximize dry-adhesive contact. Because the surface is textured and potentially porous or non-flat, adhesion is significantly degraded, shifting the burden of lifting toward frictional support and requiring a higher normal force command from the controller. Without authoritative mass measurements, the estimate is scaled toward the higher end of the moderate range based purely on the suboptimal surface condition for gecko pads.
